intro: The best-fit line balances residuals while minimizing their squared total. Centering separates the slope calculation from the choice of intercept.
task: Compute ordinary least-squares slope/intercept and residual sum of squares for paired observations.
requirements: inputs and targets are equal-length vectors with at least two observations. The sum of squared centered inputs must be >=1e-10.
Return {"slope", "intercept", "residuals", "squared_error"} for the unweighted least-squares line with an intercept.
Residuals are target minus prediction. Use centered inputs to compute slope; preserve observation order.

Unless a requirement explicitly sets another range, numeric inputs are real and finite with magnitude at most 10000. Booleans are rejected except explicit boolean masks. Vectors have length 1..64 and matrix axes 1..64 unless specified otherwise. Leave inputs unchanged. Raise ValueError for invalid types, bounds, shapes or documented domain conditions.

examples.output:

hints.title: Choose the representation
hints.body: Center both vectors before forming their cross-product and input squared norm.

hints.title: Build the result
hints.body: Recover the intercept from the two means, then evaluate predictions and residuals in original order.

explanation: The best-fit line balances residuals while minimizing their squared total. Centering separates the slope calculation from the choice of intercept.
With an intercept, residuals sum to approximately zero and are orthogonal to centered inputs. These identities check the fit independently of repeating the closed-form formula.
